articles.title: 'Frango não tem partido': agro defende equilíbrio após eleição | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialistas dizem que alinhamento político com os EUA não pode afastar o país de Pequim. China é a maior compradora do agro brasileiro e tem investimentos em infraestrutura estratégica para as exportações.
articles.summary: Larissa Wachholz afirma que a preocupação chinesa com a região cresceu sob Trump. Especialistas defendem que o Brasil preserve relações com Pequim e Washington.
articles.body:
Post do porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da China sobre o Brasil — Foto: X / Reprodução

"A China tem olhado para a América Latina com muita cautela, buscando observar onde o seu investimento é bem-vindo, onde as suas relações comerciais são bem-vindas e onde não são."

A análise é da especialista em China Larissa Wachholz, que foi assessora especial do Ministério da Agricultura entre 2019 e 2021. Ela participou de um evento no Insper, em São Paulo, sobre o futuro da segurança alimentar no país e os impactos para o agronegócio brasileiro, na quarta-feira (7).

Questionada pelo g1 , ela analisou como Pequim vê o resultado do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial, que terminou com o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) à frente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT).

A cautela chinesa está ligada à possibilidade de o Brasil e outros países da América Latina se alinharem mais aos Estados Unidos, sob o governo de Donald Trump . Ela afirma que essa preocupação começou no primeiro mandato do republicano e se intensificou no segundo.

"Os Estados Unidos têm deixado cada vez mais claro em seus documentos internos que eles veem a América Latina como uma região de influência norte-americana", disse ela.

"Eles [os chineses] não querem se estabelecer em locais de confronto porque isso impõe um risco muito grande. Os investimentos precisam fazer sentido econômico e eles só vão fazer se houver estabilidade jurídica", destacou Wachholz, que coordena o Programa Ásia, no Centro Brasileiro de Relações Internacionais (Cebri).

Os presidentes da América do Sul alinhados com Donald Trump. — Foto: Elaboração g1

Para o agronegócio brasileiro, os investimentos chineses têm ajudado a superar gargalos de infraestrutura e a tornar os produtos nacionais mais competitivos no exterior. Um exemplo está na estrutura necessária para exportar carnes: a carga precisa ser mantida refrigerada durante o transporte, o que exige contêineres especiais e portos preparados para operá-los.

"Hoje, nós temos investimentos importantes da China nessa área, que é o que acaba viabilizando a nossa exportação tão competitiva", ressalta.

"Por isso, se é de interesse do Brasil continuar atraindo investimentos chineses, é importante fazer uma sinalização positiva para a China e não sinalizar confronto. Mesmo que a gente tenha, eventualmente, um governo mais alinhado com os Estados Unidos, ", afirma.

Um exemplo é a participação da chinesa Cofco no terminal STS11, no Porto de Santos (SP), usado para a exportação de produtos agrícolas.

Já em Paranaguá (PR), a TCP, controlada pela chinesa China Merchants Port, ampliou a estrutura de tomadas para contêineres refrigerados, usados no transporte de carnes e outros alimentos congelados. Concluída em 2024, a expansão aumentou a capacidade de armazenar essas cargas e mantê-las na temperatura adequada até o embarque.

A avaliação de Wachholz é compartilhada por Marcos Jank, coordenador do Insper Agro Global, e Ricardo Santin, presidente da Associação Brasileira de Proteína Animal (ABPA), que também participaram do debate.

"Vou dar a mesma resposta que eu dei quando o [Jair] Bolsonaro saiu do governo. Frango não tem partido nem ideologia. Não dá para misturar isso. Isso é muito importante. O agronegócio trabalha para a segurança alimentar brasileira e de 170 países. Então não tem não tem governo que vai atrapalhar um negócio que representa 35% do PIB brasileiro", afirmou o presidente da ABPA.

Para ele, o peso do Brasil no abastecimento mundial exige que qualquer governante preserve as relações comerciais com os países compradores. Santin afirmou ainda que não espera mudanças nas exportações de carnes para a China por causa do resultado eleitoral.

Já Marcos Jank destacou que a política comercial de Trump, marcada pela imposição de tarifas a outros países, tornou o ambiente internacional mais complexo para os negócios nos últimos anos.

Para ele, esse cenário exige que o Brasil preserve as relações com as duas potências: uma maior afinidade política com Washington ou Pequim não deveria significar o afastamento do outro parceiro.

“Nós temos que nos dar bem com os Estados Unidos e com a China, ou seja, isso é obrigatório”, afirmou.

A China é a maior compradora de produtos agropecuários do Brasil, seguida da União Europeia e dos Estados Unidos, segundo dados do Ministério da Agricultura.

articles.title: Por que as eleições mexem tanto com dólar e bolsa?  | G1
articles.standfirst: O g1 analisou o comportamento do dólar e do Ibovespa desde 1994 para mostrar como eleições e crises políticas mexeram com os mercados. Especialistas explicam o que está por trás das oscilações e como investir em períodos de maior volatilidade.
articles.summary: Pesquisas, propostas e resultados das urnas podem mudar as expectativas dos investidores; veja o histórico desde 1994 e saiba como lidar com períodos de maior volatilidade.
articles.body:
B3, bolsa de valores brasileira. — Foto: Divulgação/ B3

Antes mesmo de os brasileiros irem às urnas no último domingo (4), as eleições já estavam no radar dos mercados. Desde o começo do ano, foram vários os momentos de altas e baixas no dólar, na bolsa e nas taxas de juros, associados a falas de candidatos e pesquisas eleitorais.

As movimentações refletem as apostas do mercado sobre os rumos da economia no próximo governo. Não à toa, o resultado do 1º turno já teve impacto no dólar e no Ibovespa.

Na segunda-feira (5), um dia após a apuração das urnas mostrar Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) à frente, com 47,03% dos votos válidos, ante 45,16% de Lula ( PT ), o dólar caiu mais de 4% e terminou o dia cotado a R$ 5, o menor patamar desde maio.

Já a bolsa brasileira disparou 7,70%, na maior alta diária desde março de 2020, e fechou no recorde de 206.912 pontos .

“Os preços refletem expectativas sobre crescimento, inflação, juros e, no Brasil, sobretudo a trajetória fiscal. A eleição deixa essas variáveis em aberto, e cada pesquisa ou declaração muda as probabilidades de cada cenário”, explica o chefe de investimentos do ASA, Rogerio Freitas.

Por que as eleições mexem com dólar, bolsa e juros?

O mercado costuma sofrer grandes oscilações em momentos como esse porque tenta antecipar os efeitos que as propostas e as chances de vitória de cada candidato podem ter sobre a economia.

Dados históricos mostram que o Ibovespa, o dólar e os juros futuros costumam reagir com maior intensidade em períodos eleitorais e diante de notícias políticas , principalmente quando aumentam as incertezas sobre as contas públicas e os rumos da economia.

🔎 Os efeitos aparecem de formas diferentes em cada mercado. A bolsa reage às expectativas dos investidores para a economia e para o desempenho das empresas. Já o dólar responde à percepção de risco e aos movimentos de entrada e saída de recursos do país.

Recentemente, a notícia de reajuste do Bolsa Família, anunciado pelo governo Lula a 17 dias das eleições presidenciais, fez o real se desvalorizar em relação ao dólar e a bolsa brasileira cair aos 185 mil pontos, com as preocupações com o impacto do aumento do benefício sobre as contas públicas.

Da mesma forma, pesquisas eleitorais divulgadas nos últimos meses, que mostraram um avanço de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) na disputa, também tiveram repercussão nos mercados.

Em 10 de setembro, uma pesquisa que mostrou Flávio numericamente à frente de Lula (PT) em uma eventual disputa de segundo turno coincidiu com queda de 0,18% do dólar, a R$ 5,1026 , e alta de 1,42% do Ibovespa, aos 188.268 pontos.

Como o g1 mostrou, uma eventual vitória de Flávio é vista pelo mercado financeiro como mais favorável ao equilíbrio das contas públicas . Essa expectativa tende a reduzir as taxas de juros projetadas para os próximos anos e a aumentar o interesse por investimentos no Brasil, o que beneficia a bolsa e o real.

“A volatilidade tende a crescer perto das eleições, mas os primeiros atos do eleito pesam mais que o discurso de campanha. Mas cada eleição precisa ser lida no seu próprio contexto”, diz Freitas, do ASA.

Essa maior volatilidade, no entanto, não se limita aos períodos eleitorais. O noticiário político também pode mexer com os mercados, especialmente quando envolve medidas capazes de afetar a inflação, os juros e a atividade econômica.

“Há períodos em que, mesmo diante de escândalos políticos, outros fatores pesam mais, como o fluxo de capital estrangeiro para o país”, afirma Alvaro Maia, banker da StoneX. O analista lembra que o Mensalão, em 2006, teve forte repercussão política , mas influência limitada sobre os mercados.

“Isso porque havia mais dinheiro circulando nos mercados internacionais, os bancos no exterior estavam mais dispostos a emprestar recursos, as commodities estavam em alta e as ações brasileiras eram negociadas a preços relativamente baixos em relação aos resultados das empresas. Então, a política acabou ficando um pouco em segundo plano”, explica Maia.

Abaixo, o g1 mostra o histórico das cotações do dólar e do Ibovespa desde 1994, com destaque para alguns períodos de maior oscilação. Em seguida, confira dicas para investir em momentos de maior volatilidade.

Histórico do dólar e do Ibovespa de 1994 a 2026. — Foto: Arte/g1

Como investir em momentos de volatilidade?

Na hora de investir, uma das recomendações é recorrer à renda fixa para atravessar períodos de maior volatilidade com mais segurança.

“Em um momento em que temos juros em dois dígitos, a renda fixa está especialmente atrativa. São várias opções, com destaque para os títulos públicos prefixados ou para os fundos de renda fixa”, comenta Maia.

Para quem planeja investir na bolsa de valores, a recomendação é evitar montar uma carteira de ações com base em pesquisas eleitorais ou em apostas sobre o resultado das urnas.

“O melhor é manter a estratégia de longo prazo e fazer ajustes na carteira sem agir por impulso. Grande parte do resultado vem da forma como os investimentos são distribuídos”, diz Freitas.

“Diversificar, inclusive no exterior, ajuda a reduzir riscos, enquanto uma reserva de fácil acesso evita que o investidor precise vender ativos em momentos de queda. O tempo é o maior aliado”, completa.

Outro cuidado é adequar a carteira ao perfil de cada investidor e à sua tolerância ao risco. Quem tem um perfil mais conservador, por exemplo, tende a concentrar uma parcela maior dos recursos em investimentos menos sujeitos a oscilações. Já quem aceita correr mais riscos pode ter uma fatia maior em ativos como ações.

articles.title: Bezos says Blue Origin likely to pursue IPO in coming years
articles.summary: Oct 7 (Reuters) - Blue Origin is likely to pursue an initial public offering in the coming years, billionaire founder Jeff Bezos said on Wednesday, after the...
articles.body:
Oct 7 (Reuters) - Blue Origin is likely to pursue an initial public offering in the coming years, billionaire ‌founder Jeff Bezos said on Wednesday, after the space ‌company raised $10 billion from outside investors for the first time in a funding ​round.

"I think, someday, Blue Origin will have an IPO... It would be several years from now. But it probably makes sense for Blue Origin to be a public company at some point," Bezos ‌said on FOX News ⁠Channel's "Special Report with Bret Baier".

The remarks are Bezos' clearest indication yet that Blue Origin could seek ⁠a stock market listing. An eventual IPO would offer investors exposure to a major space company amid renewed interest in the sector, ​though rival ​SpaceX, which listed in June, ​remains the dominant player.

Bezos, ‌who also founded Amazon.com, said he has personally invested $28 billion in Blue Origin since establishing the company in 2000.

The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Blue Origin's recent funding round valued it at $140 billion.

Founded about 18 months before Elon Musk's SpaceX, ‌Blue Origin has largely relied on ​Bezos for funding while securing multibillion-dollar NASA ​and US Space Force ​contracts, including for work on the Artemis lunar ‌program.

Blue Origin aims to resume ​New Glenn launches ​this year after a launch-pad explosion during a static-fire test in May delayed its efforts to compete with SpaceX ​in the commercial ‌launch market.

"December of this year, we're going to fly that ​vehicle again," Bezos said.

(Reporting by Mrinmay Dey in Mexico ​City; Editing by Subhranshu Sahu)

articles.title: Javi Linares, asesor financiero: "El coche que puedes pagar quizás no es el que puedes permitirte; debería representar entre el 10% y el 15% de tus ingresos netos"
articles.standfirst: El experto analiza el mercado y alerta sobre las cuotas mensuales
articles.summary: El experto analiza el mercado y alerta sobre las cuotas mensuales
articles.body: Comprarse un coche es un paso muy importante para cualquier persona. Joven o adulto, es algo a tener en cuenta porque el desembolso de dinero es elevado. Y no sólo por la compra como tal, sino porque vienen asociados otros gastos, como el seguro, el combustible, mantenimiento o cualquier otro tipo de coste financiero. Además de la depreciación. Precisamente por todos esos gastos ‘extra’, más allá del precio final del coche, hacen que haya que tener cuidado. No todo se reduce únicamente a la cuota mensual a pagar, o al importe de entrada. Y eso es precisamente lo que alertan los expertos, que tratan de dar algunos ‘trucos’ para que la salud financiera de la población no se resienta por comprar, en este caso, automóviles que no deberían poder pagar. “El coche que puedes pagarte no es necesariamente el coche que te puedes permitir”, ha especificado Javi Linares, asesor financiero. Para eso, hay que ver muchas cosas, sobre todo con vistas a que dichos gastos no se descontrolen. El coste total del vehículo debe estar siempre en el punto de mira, tal y como reconoce el asesor. Pero hay más: ¿cuánto dinero entra al mes? ¿Cuánto se ahorra y qué margen queda con los gastos fijos? De acuerdo con sus referencias, el coste total del vehículo, que no solo la cuota, debe estar entre el 10% y el 15% de los ingresos netos. E, incluso, va un paso más allá en sus predicciones. “La cuota es la peor brújula que existe: está diseñada para que casi cualquier coche te encaje”, ha especificado. Por lo tanto, la situación debería medirse de manera diferente. No tratar de hacer un presupuesto en busca de comprarse un coche, sino saber qué dinero puedes destinar íntegramente al pago del vehículo, para que tu salud financiera no se resienta de ninguna manera con ello.

articles.title: Jim Cramer Says SPCX Could Come to Fruition Long Before Tesla After Goldman Sachs Raises Price Target: 'Real Company With Real Numbers'
articles.summary: TV Host Jim Cramer has praised Elon Musk‘s commercial spaceflight company Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX), saying that the enterprise coul...
articles.body:
TV Host Jim Cramer has praised Elon Musk 's commercial spaceflight company Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ: SPCX ), saying that the enterprise could benefit investors even before Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA ) did.

SpaceX Is a 'Real Company' With a 'Real Business'

On Wednesday, Cramer hailed SpaceX on the "Mad Money" show on CNBC, saying that Musk had made some "very smart moves" by renting out excess AI compute with NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ: NVDA ) chips that Cramer said Musk bought at "extortionate prices," while also pointing to the compute deals with Anthropic and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) (NASDAQ: GOOG ).

"I've been adamant this [SpaceX] is a real company with real numbers and a real business, many businesses even," Cramer said, adding that he had defended the company against criticism that it was overvalued .

Cramer then pointed to Goldman Sachs Group Inc. (NYSE: GS ) raising its price target for SpaceX to $230, which "ratified" the previous $220 price target. "When you're dealing with real speculative games, you almost never see price target bumps until after the hot money's over on the price target. By then, it's too late anyway," Cramer said.

However, Cramer then said that he understood the investment bank's price target bump, adding that SpaceX was making "so much money renting out compute" that it was planning to borrow $40 billion to buy more NVIDIA chips .

"SpaceX could end up being NVIDIA's largest client at this pace. That's fantastic news for both sides," he said. The TV Host then said that it was "becoming more and more likely that SpaceX could come to fruition a lot earlier than Tesla ever did."

Notably, Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS ) analyst Adam Jonas said that the company presented a "unique" investment opportunity with its wide array of "interlinked" businesses and that it was "unusually cheap" when investors factored in the opportunities in chipmaking and power.

Jonas reiterated an "overweight" rating for SpaceX and issued a price target of $300 for SpaceX shares, illustrating bullish sentiment on the stock.

Price Action: SPCX shares were up 0.27% to $168.05 during overnight trading on Wednesday.

articles.title: AI Bubble Risks Worst S&P 500 Crash Since 2008, Strategist Says
articles.summary: The head of market strategy at a London investment bank has a stark warning for investors: the artificial-intelligence trade may soon be over in what could t...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The head of market strategy at a London investment bank has a stark warning for investors: the artificial-intelligence trade may soon be over in what could trigger the most severe market crash since the global financial crisis.

Equities have powered to record levels across the globe this year, fueled in part by optimism over surging spending on AI infrastructure. But Panmure Liberum's Joachim Klement said his base case is for that trade to disintegrate as soon as 2027, sending stocks sharply lower.

"My core conviction is that the AI bubble will either burst in 2027 or in 2028, so sometime in the next two years," Klement said in an interview. Hyperscalers' free cash flows are largely depleted, while the cost of debt is rising quickly and becoming prohibitive for these firms, he said.

Klement's 2027 year-end target of 5,000 points for the S&P 500 implies 36% downside from current levels. That's by far the most bearish of seven other strategists tracked by Bloomberg, who on average look for potential upside of 14%. Klement sees Europe's Stoxx 600 falling to 430 points, more than 30% below current levels.

The strategist, who started his career at UBS Group AG more than two decades ago, is among the first to call an end to the stock market's current bull run. As recently as mid-September, his key assumption was that the S&P 500 would hit 8,300 points by the end of next year.

His change of mind reflects concern that stubborn inflation and an associated surge in the cost of borrowing needed to fund investment could derail the bonanza in AI-related infrastructure.

That echoes a warning this week from Temasek International's chief investment officer Rohit Sipahimalani that a reversal of the AI trade is a key risk facing global markets.

Data-center capital spending by hyperscalers in 2026 could more than double from last year's level to hit $713 billion, according to Bloomberg Intelligence estimates. That number is set to increase further next year, albeit at a slower pace, and has underpinned many of the projections for US tech companies' projected earnings.

"It is a situation where people are just focusing on one thing and one thing only, and that is earnings and in particular tech earnings," Klement said. "And they excuse every macro, credit or whatever headwind that you can come up with with that story."

articles.title: When support matters most: How Policybazaar helps customers navigate medical emergencies
articles.summary: Buying a good comprehensive health insurance policy is just the start.
articles.body: Buying a good comprehensive health insurance policy is just the start. The real test comes during a medical emergency, when families face hospital chaos, treatment decisions, procedural red tape, and the clock ticking on your finances. That’s where most policyholders are left scrambling alone.Not at Policybazaar.In FY26, Policybazaar navigated over 3.75 lakh insurance claims, including more than 2.45 lakh health insurance claims, serving as the crucial bridge between patients and payouts. Every single day, its specialized claims team fields more than 7,000 interactions: documentation handholding, hospital negotiations, relentless follow-throughs. Not only that, Policybazaar successfully intervened to get 11,156 rejected health insurance claims reconsidered and paid out over the past year, working closely with our insurance partners.Because Policybazaar’s support at the ‘moment of truth’ is what sets us apart, especially when families need guidance and timely assistance during a claim. When hospitals won't wait. When TPAs demand more documents. That's when timely expertise, domain knowledge, and sheer persistence become the difference between financial catastrophe and recovery.Racing against time for a cancer patientWhen Policybazaar customer Prakash Dixit reached out in March 2026, he was deeply distressed. His mother's chemotherapy claim had been rejected because the insurer was unable to establish the duration of her illness.The situation was urgent. Her next chemotherapy session was scheduled within six days, with each treatment costing nearly Rs 80,000. Delaying treatment was not an option, while paying for it themselves was beyond the family's means.Policybazaar's claims team immediately began reviewing the medical records to understand why the claim had been declined. During the review, they identified an earlier consultation that established the timeline of the illness, an important medical detail that had not been adequately considered during the initial assessment. Armed with this evidence, the team escalated the case to the insurer's medical panel and requested an expedited review, given the patient's next chemotherapy session was only days away.Within hours, the insurer partner completed a fresh assessment, approved the claim in full and also cleared future chemotherapy treatments. For the family, the outcome meant they could focus on recovery instead of worrying about arranging funds."At a time when we were only thinking about my mother's treatment, the Policybazaar team took ownership of everything else. We will always be grateful for the support," Dixit later shared with the team.Going beyond paperwork during a stroke emergencyFor Subhash Yadav and his wife, Anu Yadav, the crisis came unexpectedly.Just months after porting their health insurance policy through Policybazaar, Yadav suffered a severe brain stroke and was rushed to Kailash Hospital, Noida, where he was diagnosed with a subdural haemorrhage. When the hospital raised a cashless request, the insurer declined it, citing concerns over a possible undisclosed medical history because the policy had recently been ported.Despite repeated clarifications from the hospital and treating doctors, the claim continued to be denied.When the family approached Policybazaar, the company's medical panel reviewed every clinical document to understand the insurer partner's concerns and pinpointed the precise evidence required to address them. Rather than leaving the family to gather the paperwork themselves, a Policybazaar representative visited the hospital, worked alongside the treating team and hospital administration, collected the missing clinical records and ensured the insurer received a complete medical submission.Once the additional information was submitted, our insurance partner reassessed the case and approved the cashless claim. The approval meant the family could concentrate on his treatment instead of worrying about arranging funds during an already stressful time."We had almost given up hope. The Policybazaar team stayed with us through the process until the approval finally came," recalled Anu Yadav.Correcting one medical detail saved a Rs 20 lakh claimAnother case involved Sayyed Hussain, a 34-year-old customer who was hospitalised with kidney failure and also suffered a heart attack within a year of purchasing his health insurance policy.The estimated treatment cost was around Rs 20 lakh. However, the insurer initially rejected the claim because the duration of his chronic kidney disease had been incorrectly recorded by the treating doctor.When Hussain's sister approached Policybazaar for help, the claims team immediately stepped in. Instead of accepting the rejection at face value, the team reconstructed the patient's medical history from the available records. During this review, they discovered that the duration of the illness had been incorrectly recorded in the medical documents. The first consultation letter clearly established that the diagnosis had actually been made after the policy was issued, fundamentally changing the insurer's assessment of the claim.Armed with this medical evidence, Policybazaar escalated the matter with the insurer and remained closely engaged until the case was reassessed. Following a detailed review, the insurer approved the claim, covering multiple hospitalisations worth nearly Rs 20 lakh."Knowing someone was fighting for us during such a difficult time meant everything," Hussain's sister later told the Policybazaar team after his recovery.Standing by customers beyond the policy purchaseFor most people, buying health insurance is a one-time decision. But the real experience begins when a claim has to be made.These are just a few of the many instances where Policybazaar stood by its customers and helped them navigate challenging situations. It often requires careful scrutiny of medical records, timely intervention, close engagement with hospitals and insurers, and persistent follow-through until a genuine claim reaches a fair outcome. While claim decisions remain with insurers and are subject to policy terms and conditions, timely intervention and accurate documentation can often make a meaningful difference.Behind every claim is a family looking for reassurance during a difficult time. These stories reflect Policybazaar's commitment to standing by its customers long after the policy has been purchased, helping them navigate one of life's most stressful moments with confidence and care.References: article has been contributed by Amit Chhabra, Chief Business Officer, General Insurance, Policybazaar.Disclaimer - The above content is non-editorial, and TIL hereby disclaims any and all warranties, expressed or implied, relating to it, and does not guarantee, vouch for or necessarily endorse any of the content.You use AI every day. articles.title: Retired bank employee got Rs 12.27 lakh leave encashment and claimed Rs 3 lakh exemption in 2020, but government later hiked limit to Rs 25 lakh in 2023; ITAT Chennai allows full tax exemption
articles.summary: You retire and get leave encashment, a part of which is exempt from tax.
articles.body: You retire and get leave encashment, a part of which is exempt from tax. You file your income tax return claiming the exemption, but later the exemption limit is hiked. Are you entitled to the benefits of the enhanced leave encashment exemption limit?In one such case, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Chennai has given its decision in favour of a retired bank employee.The case involved a question that has come up before several tax tribunals: whether the higher leave-encashment exemption introduced in 2023 can also benefit employees who retired before that change, particularly when their tax proceedings were still being pursued.What the case is aboutThe taxpayer had retired from a bank during the financial year 2019-20. On superannuation, he received Rs 12,27,232 as leave encashment.When he filed his income tax return for assessment year 2020-21 on September 10, 2020, he claimed Rs 3 lakh as exempt under Section 10(10AA)(ii) of the Income Tax Act. After claiming that exemption, he declared a total income of Rs 24,36,260.Also Read | US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary propertyAt that time, the exemption ceiling for leave encashment applicable to non-government employees was Rs 3 lakh. The man accordingly claimed exemption of Rs 3 lakh when he filed his income tax return.Subsequently, a CBDT Notification No. 31/2023 dated 24 May 2023 increased the exemption limit for non-government employees from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 25 lakh.The notification stated that it would come into force from 1 April 2023, while its Explanatory Memorandum records that no person would be adversely affected by giving retrospective effect to the notification.That change prompted the man to seek the benefit of the higher exemption against his earlier claim. Since he had received only Rs 12.27 lakh, he sought exemption for the entire amount, rather than the Rs 3 lakh he had originally claimed.His return had already been processed by the Centralised Processing Centre (CPC), Bengaluru, under Section 143(1) on December 13, 2020. The CPC had allowed the Rs 3 lakh exemption and brought the balance leave encashment to tax.The man subsequently appealed against the CPC's order before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) on January 7, 2026. The CIT(A), however, rejected his claim on February 25, 2026. It held that the notification applicable to assessment year 2020-21 was the earlier notification that prescribed the Rs 3 lakh ceiling.The man then approached the Chennai ITAT.Also Read | Man deposits Rs 85.3 lakh received as cash gifts from wife, relatives; income tax calls it unexplained and sends notice, but ITAT Chennai accepts gift deeds and gives reliefWhy did ITAT rule in favour of the retired employee?The key question before the ITAT was whether the enhanced limit could benefit an employee who had retired before 1 April 2023. The Tribunal answered this in the affirmative.Before ITAT, it was argued that the 2023 enhancement was beneficial and curative. Although the notification specified April 1, 2023 as its effective date, the taxpayer argued that its explanatory memorandum and the nature of the amendment supported its application to his case.The Tribunal began by identifying the central issue: whether the man was entitled to exemption up to Rs 25 lakh under Section 10(10AA)(ii), or whether the exemption for his assessment year had to remain restricted to Rs 3 lakh.The bench noted that Section 10(10AA)(ii) already provided an exemption for leave encashment received by non-government employees, subject to a monetary ceiling notified by the Central Government.According to Amit Ganatra, Executive Director, Khaitan & Co, ITAT’s reasoning was principally founded on the beneficial and remedial character of the CBDT notification.“The ITAT noted that the notification did not create a new exemption or introduce a new class of eligible taxpayers; rather, it enhanced the monetary ceiling of an exemption which was already available to non-government employees under section 10(10AA)(ii),” Ganatra tells TOI.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claimsThe earlier ceiling of Rs 3 lakh had remained unchanged for almost 20 years, despite substantial changes in salary levels and the economic environment.“ITAT therefore viewed the enhancement to Rs 25 lakh as a measure intended to update and rationalise an existing provision and to mitigate the hardship arising from the continued application of an outdated monetary limit. ITAT also considered it inequitable to deny the benefit of the enhanced ceiling to employees merely because their retirement preceded the date on which the notification was issued, particularly where the benefit was otherwise intended to address the inadequacy of the earlier limit,” he said.A significant factor considered by the ITAT was the Explanatory Memorandum accompanying Notification No. 31/2023. While the notification itself provides that it shall come into force from 1 April 2023, the Explanatory Memorandum specifically states that “no person is being adversely affected by giving retrospective effect to the notification”.ITAT held that provisions intended to confer a benefit and remove hardship should be interpreted liberally and, in appropriate cases, applied retrospectively, particularly where doing so did not adversely affect any vested right of the Revenue.The bench also said the absence of an express retrospective clause could not by itself settle the issue when the amendment merely enlarged an existing benefit. In its view, the remedial nature of the change had to be considered.Ganatra explained that ITAT relied on this to ascertain the remedial intent underlying the enhancement. In such circumstances, the absence of an express provision giving retrospective effect was not considered determinative, particularly since the notification merely enlarged the monetary limit of an existing exemption.ITAT also noted the settled judicial principle that beneficial and curative amendments may be applied in appropriate cases to advance the cause of justice.Ganatra says that another important factor was the judicial consistency emerging from various ITAT benches.“The Chennai Bench referred to a number of earlier decisions which had similarly allowed the enhanced Rs 25 lakh limit in cases involving earlier retirement years. ITAT therefore considered its conclusion to be supported by a developing line of coordinate-bench decisions,” he said.After considering the statutory provision, the notification, the explanatory material and the earlier ITAT decisions, the Chennai ITAT held that the man was entitled to the enhanced Rs 25 lakh limit.Because his leave encashment was Rs 12,27,232, the entire amount was below the enhanced ceiling and therefore eligible for exemption.The Tribunal consequently set aside the restriction imposed by the CPC and the order of the CIT(A). It directed the Assessing Officer to allow the exemption claimed by the man.Also Read | Man opted for VRS after employer shut plant, got Rs 65.21 lakh and reported it as advance salary in ITR; Section 89 relief was denied, but ITAT Pune later ruled it a non-taxable capital receiptSignificance for taxpayersThe Khaitan & Co expert says that for taxpayers, the ruling is particularly relevant to non-government employees who retired before 1 April 2023 and whose exemption for leave encashment was restricted to Rs 3 lakh.“The decision provides judicial support for the position that the enhanced exemption limit of Rs 25 lakh may also be available in respect of such earlier years,” he says.However, he cautions that the issue is not free from judicial divergence.“In Purnendu Shekhar Sinha v. Union of India, the Patna High Court, while examining the constitutional validity of the distinction under section 10(10AA) between employees of the Central/State Governments and employees of other establishments, held that such classification was not discriminatory and proceeded on the basis that 1 April 2023 is the operative date for the enhanced exemption limit,” he says.“This judgement was not brought to the notice of the Chennai ITAT. Accordingly, while the Chennai ITAT ruling strengthens the case for retrospective application of the enhanced limit, the issue cannot, at this stage, be regarded as conclusively settled for all taxpayers,” he adds.You use AI every day. articles.title: Es oficial: se plantea la jubilación anticipada a los trabajadores que tengan 40 años cotizados pero las elecciones lo pueden retrasar
articles.standfirst: Los comicios marcarán los tiempos de esta medida
articles.summary: Los comicios marcarán los tiempos de esta medida
articles.body: La convocatoria de elecciones generales para el próximo 29 de noviembre de 2026 va a tener consecuencias no sólo para el calendario político de España, también va a afectar a otros campos, como por ejemplo la economía. De hecho, la jubilación anticipada para quienes tengan 40 años cotizados y tramitada por el Congreso podría sufrir retrasos debido a la celebración de estos comicios. Cabe recordar que, de cara a 2027, será necesario haber cotizado 38 años y seis meses para poder jubilarse a los 65 años, ya que quienes no cumplan con ellos lo harán a los 67 años. Dado que es necesario cumplir con esos dos requisitos para el retiro a la edad ordinaria, muchos se ven obligados a superar la cotización a los 40 años y sin poder jubilarse. Para evitar estas largas carreras, el Congreso aprobó la propuesta de ley para que estas personas puedan jubilarse, sin que haya penalizaciones. Si quieren el retiro a los 63, sí se contemplan reducciones que, en algunos casos, llegan al 21%. Por ahora, eso sí, es una propuesta de ley y aún deberá pasar a ser ley y entrar en vigor, y es ahí precisamente donde entra en juego el asunto de las elecciones generales. Dado que se han convocado los comicios para el 29 de noviembre y las Cortes han quedado disueltas, tal y como marca la normativa, los tiempos para las votaciones van a cambiar por completo. Ya no es posible someter a debate esto y, por tanto, será necesaria la conformación de nuevas Cortes. Sólo una vez se establezca un nuevo Congreso y Senado, será cuando esta y otras propuestas de ley puedan ser votadas y comprobar si, efectivamente, esta medida para las largas carreras de cotización sale adelante o si, por el contrario, sufre modificaciones por parte del partido que alcance el poder en esas elecciones.

articles.title: Russia eyes return to Europe's gas market despite sanctions, Ukraine war: Report
articles.summary: Russia may be looking to turn the gas taps to Europe back on, with talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once
articles.body: Russia may be looking to turn the gas taps to Europe back on, with talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once carried Russian gas to Germany.According to five people familiar with the matter, the discussions involve US Special Envoy Jared Kushner and Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin.Kushner, who has been trying to broker a truce between Russia and Ukraine, sees business deals as central to restoring peace. A potential Nord Stream deal could allow US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe once the war ends.Nord Stream back on the tableKushner and Dmitriev have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks. Two sources told Reuters that Nord Stream remains on the agenda, although not much details are available about the discussions.Dmitriev, who has been pushing for Russian gas sales to Germany to resume, met representatives of the US energy and treasury departments last month, to discuss potential US-Russia energy initiatives.A White House official said that any deals would have to be negotiated with the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Treasury and must benefit US taxpayers and companies."Any deals will have to be negotiated by Russia with DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) and Treasury and must benefit United States taxpayers and companies," the official said.The official also said there had been "no Nord Stream discussions recently".Restarting gas flows won't be easyA return of Russian gas to Germany still faces several hurdles. The Nord Stream pipelines are sanctioned by the US and the EU, making any restart illegal.A US official said a deal was unlikely in the medium term because of the obstacles involved. US President Donald Trump could waive or soften US sanctions, but that would become harder if Democrats win control of Congress in next month's midterm elections.Germany and other European countries are also expected to oppose reopening Nord Stream. They are spending billions of euros rebuilding their military to defend themselves from Russia.A spokeswoman for Germany's economy and energy ministry said Nord Stream and Russian gas were sanctioned in Europe and that Germany had found alternatives. She said reopening the pipelines would require government approval and was not desired.Before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Germany bought more than half of its gas from Russia through the two Nord Stream pipelines. They were mothballed after Moscow throttled supplies to Europe and were blown up in a series of underwater explosions in September 2022.Germany split over Russian gasThe idea of bringing Russian gas back to Germany has also divided opinion within the country.Germany's coalition government is opposed to restarting the pipeline, while Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country's most popular political party, wants to reopen it. Dmitriev is due to meet AfD leadership early next year to discuss selling Russian gas again.Poland is also watching the discussions but remains firmly opposed to reopening the pipeline, according to one person familiar with the government's thinking. Poland and the Baltic states are particularly vulnerable to Russia and reject energy ties.The talks are taking place against a backdrop of deep European mistrust of Russia's motives. Earlier this year, the heads of five European spy agencies told Reuters that Russia did not want to end the war quickly and was using US talks to push for business deals instead.Relations between Russia and Germany, which is among the biggest providers of military support to Ukraine, have hit a low ebb. Officials in Berlin have accused Russia of mounting a systematic campaign of hybrid attacks.Some German lawmakers say business deals would bolster Moscow as it pursues war with Ukraine."This threatens to be a dirty deal that will cost Europe dearly," said Michael Kellner, a lawmaker who was in charge of German energy policy in the aftermath of the Ukraine invasion."Americans and Russians will share the profits," he said.Who owns Nord Stream?Ownership could be another hurdle for any US investment in Nord Stream.Russian state energy giant Gazprom owns 51% of the company. Another 31% is split between two German entities, while the remaining stake is held by a French and a Dutch firm.The two German shareholders want to retain their stakes to maintain German influence if Gazprom sells its share, another person familiar with the matter said.Days after the Moscow meetings, Kushner said in Kyiv that he had spoken to European counterparts about how the war had pushed up energy prices. He advocated "prosperity agreements" to encourage peace and give "leaders ... something to look forward to".Lukoil assets also in focusKushner and Dmitriev have also discussed the possible sale of businesses owned by Russian energy company Lukoil, including oil refineries and petrol stations in Europe and elsewhere, two people familiar with the matter said.Under the proposal, a consortium involving the DFC and investors from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates would buy the assets, while US authorities would lift sanctions, the people said."On Lukoil, Steve (Witkoff) and Jared (Kushner) worked with DFC to negotiate a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States," a White House official said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex tanks over 1,000 points; Nifty50 at 22,231 - top reasons for fall
articles.summary: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50, the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade on Thursday, with both indices down over 1%.
articles.body: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50, the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade on Thursday, with both indices down over 1%. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped to 22,231 levels.At closing, Nifty50 was at 22,231.80, down 371.25 points or 1.64%. BSE Sensex was at 71,593.24, down 1,045.46 points or 1.44%. The sharp decline erased over Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.ITC, Adani Ports, IndiGo, Power Grid and Reliance Industries (RIL) were among the biggest losers on the Sensex, with their shares declining as much as 4%. On the other hand, Titan and major IT stocks such as Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies, TCS and Infosys gained up to 2%, providing some support to the benchmark index.Why is stock market down today?RBI’s policy stance changeThe RBI delivered its first rate increase in nearly four years. However, market analysts viewed the central bank’s decision to move its policy stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’, against a difficult global geopolitical backdrop, as the more significant signal for markets. Jefferies expects the RBI to raise interest rates by around 100 basis points during the current tightening cycle.Nomura also pointed to the change in stance as an unexpected development. “We believe this was aimed at anchoring inflation expectations and building a buffer against adverse global conditions. However, the message was mixed, with the MPC clarifying that “calibrated tightening” only signalled “no rate cuts”, and indicated data dependence going forward,” it added.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that the calibrated tightening stance of the RBI has implications for markets.“With two more rate hikes of 25bp each likely in this rate hiking cycle, there will be pressure on valuations rising from higher fixed income returns. Investor preferences also might shift marginally towards interest inelastic segments like pharmaceuticals,” he says.US bond yields soar to 24-year highThe global selloff in bonds intensified, sending yields to their highest levels in several years. The US 30-year bond yield climbed above 5.71%, while the yield on benchmark 10-year notes rose past 5.3%. The two-year note yield also moved close to 4.9%.Rising bond yields generally make debt markets more appealing to investors, which can increase pressure on emerging-market equities. Since bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, a sharp rise in yields indicates significant selling in the bond market.Oil jumps above $102/barrelAdding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2% to move above $102 per barrel. Investors remained worried about the security of Middle East oil supplies as attacks on shipments increased in the Gulf and around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.Tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz faced the highest number of attacks in a single week since the Iran war began earlier this year, even as Gulf producers raised exports. The increase in attacks came as crude shipments from the Gulf increased, but with greater risks and higher costs for cargoes and crews. On Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said a tanker north of Qatar had been hit by multiple projectiles, resulting in casualties.Meanwhile, US crude inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels last week to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration on Wednesday. A Reuters poll of analysts had forecast a smaller decline of 1.7 million barrels.FIIs continue to sellThe record selling spree of FIIs continues, exacerbated by the rising bond yields. Foreign investors continued their selling spree in Indian equities on Wednesday, offloading shares worth more than Rs 6,121 crore on a net basis, according to provisional NSE data. Their net selling has now reached nearly Rs 57,000 crore across nine straight sessions through Wednesday.Since the start of September, FIIs have been net sellers in 20 of the 25 trading sessions. Their sustained selling, despite brief periods of buying, has continued to weigh on Dalal Street since the Middle East war began earlier this year.VK Vijayakumar notes that a distinct and strong trend in the market in recent months has been the increasing preference for growth stocks over value stocks.“Growth stocks are being accumulated at high valuations while value stocks are languishing at fair valuations. Sustained selling in large-caps by the FIIs have contributed significantly to this trend. With the US 10-year bond yield hovering above 5.3%, FIIs will continue to sell on every rally. This will put the Nifty large-caps under pressure for some more time,” he warns.“A reversal in this trend will happen only when FIIs turn buyers, and there is no clarity on when this will happen. In brief, this frustrating period in the market might continue for some more time. Remaining invested in value stocks will be rewarded in the long run. Investors should also look at the good opportunities in fixed income in this rising rate environment,” he adds.Fed rate hike worriesMinutes from the Federal Reserve's meeting showed a split among policymakers last month over the case for raising interest rates. Some officials believed a hike was needed to contain the effects of energy and other price shocks, while a more hawkish group saw higher rates as necessary to guard against emerging inflation driven by demand.Traders currently see only an 18% probability of a rate increase later this month, while the odds of a December hike are being priced at 80%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, as cited by Reuters.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: New breast cancer drug moves closer to India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A new breast cancer drug that can help delay the disease from worsening has moved closer to India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A new breast cancer drug that can help delay the disease from worsening has moved closer to India. Camizestrant, already approved in the US, European Union, UAE and Saudi Arabia, has been recommended for import and marketing in India by a government expert panel.In a major trial, patients who switched to the drug after a change was detected in their cancer cells remained free of worsening disease for 16 months on average, compared with 9.2 months among those who continued their earlier treatment. The trial involved 315 patients and found a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.The drug is meant for adults with a common type of advanced breast cancer whose treatment has started losing effectiveness. An ESR1 mutation, which can develop during hormone treatment, can make the cancer resistant to the treatment being used.“Camizestrant could be an important new option for Indian patients with advanced breast cancer who develop an ESR1 resistance mutation during hormone treatment. A blood test can detect the mutation before the disease visibly worsens, allowing treatment to be changed earlier and potentially delaying chemotherapy,” said Dr Pragya Shukla, head of clinical oncology, Delhi State Cancer Institute.She said the bigger challenge would be making ESR1 testing affordable and accessible, particularly for patients outside major cancer centres.The recommendation was made by the Subject Expert Committee (Oncology) at its meeting at the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) headquarters on September 22. The panel noted that camizestrant addressed an unmet medical need and recommended a waiver of the local Phase III trial requirement.If ultimately approved in India, camizestrant will be available only on prescription from a medical oncologist. The company has also been asked to conduct a Phase IV clinical trial and submit its protocol to CDSCO within three months of approval.The US Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to camizestrant on September 4, 2026, based on the SERENA-6 trial. The FDA approval also carries warnings about irregular heart rhythm, slow heart rate and potential harm to an unborn baby.The September 22 oncology meeting also reviewed other cancer treatments. The panel sought additional safety data for an under-the-skin form of amivantamab for certain advanced lung cancers, permitted a Phase IV trial of durvalumab in Indian patients with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer, and approved a revised Phase IV trial of lutetium Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan with at least 80 patients. It did not waive the Phase III trial requirement for trilaciclib, citing lack of unmet need, Indian patient data and comparative evidence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: No MDR on UPI from October 15? Government considers delaying rollout of fees: Report
articles.summary: Will the rollout of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions be deferred to January 2027?
articles.body: Will the rollout of Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions be deferred to January 2027? The government may postpone the move which was scheduled to be effective from October 15, 2026, by a few months, according to a regulatory official and an industry executive familiar with the matter.Last month, the government ended the zero-fee regime for UPI by allowing merchants to be charged 0.4% on transactions above Rs 2,000. UPI is used by more than 500 million people across the country for payments ranging from roadside cups of tea to iPhones.The charge is scheduled to take effect on October 15, coinciding with the annual festive season, which runs from October through December and usually brings a significant increase in consumer spending.Sources told Reuters that the proposed postponement would prevent any disruption to retail payments during the festive period while giving payments companies additional time to prepare their systems for the new fee.Investors had regarded the fee as an important monetisation opportunity for payments companies, which were expected to receive a share of the proceeds.Shares of Indian digital payments companies fell on Thursday following reports of the possible delay. Paytm dropped 7.6%, while One Mobikwik Systems declined 7.2%.Yesterday, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said that introducing a "small fee" through the MDR is unlikely to have a "major impact" on the volume of UPI transactions."As of now, we do not see any drop in volumes. And I don't personally think that a small fee will have a major impact on the volumes," he told reporters at the central bank's headquarters.What is MDR on UPI?MDR refers to the charge paid by a merchant when accepting payments for goods or services through credit or debit cards. It is generally calculated as a percentage of the transaction amount and is deducted by the bank before the merchant receives the payment.The government has clarified that UPI will continue to be free for consumers, with no transaction fee imposed on person-to-person payments.The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) notified an MDR of 0.4% for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in September. Person-to-person payments will remain free. For transactions of Rs 75,000 or more, the MDR will be subject to a maximum charge of Rs 300 per transaction.Small-value UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000 will not be affected. These transactions account for more than 95% of the total volume of UPI P2M transactions.The objective behind introducing a reasonable MDR is to keep UPI accessible and convenient for everyday payments while also supporting the long-term sustainability of the UPI ecosystem.A gazette notification issued on September 14 specifies that banks and system providers cannot levy any fee, whether directly or indirectly, on individuals making or receiving payments through RuPay debit cards or UPI transactions of up to Rs 2,000.The notification follows an amendment to Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, which established a framework allowing Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) to be imposed on payments made through UPI and other electronic payment methods notified under the law.Parliament approved the amendment Bill during the Monsoon Session in August this year.You use AI every day. articles.standfirst: Este individuo defiende en ‘La Mesa’, de Antena 3, que los políticos no deberían responsabilizar a la ciudadanía de un problema que también les atañe a ellos
articles.summary: Este individuo defiende en ‘La Mesa’, de Antena 3, que los políticos no deberían responsabilizar a la ciudadanía de un problema que también les atañe a ellos
articles.body: En las últimas semanas, la población ha escuchado todo tipo de afirmaciones sobre fondos buitre, grandes tenedores, coleccionistas de inmuebles, etc. El problema de la vivienda sigue siendo un quebradero de cabeza para la ciudadanía y el Gobierno parece haber encontrado culpables. Javier Medina, inversor de 32 años con 11 pisos, entraría dentro de la descripción que se ha ido compartiendo. De hecho, el ministro Óscar Puente lo señaló en sus redes sociales, con un tuit que decía que “era la mejor pedagogía para entender lo que está sucediendo y el perverso marco legal que tenemos”. Lo extraño para Medina no es el señalamiento en sí, sino el origen del mismo. Y es que, a su juicio, la mayoría de políticos no son muy distintos a él en asuntos inmobiliarios. “Pedro Sánchez cobra más de 12.000 euros en rentas. La mujer del presidente del Gobierno tiene en propiedad viviendas. El 42% de los diputados tiene, al menos, dos viviendas o más. En el Senado, el grupo socialista tiene más del 50% viviendas en propiedad. ¿Cómo puede esta gente echarnos la culpa a nosotros? Dejan la responsabilidad que tendrían que asumir ellos”, enumera tajante Medina. Tampoco se limita a la hora de hablar de Óscar Puente, después del tuit que le dedicó. En su opinión, una persona con “tanta responsabilidad en el Gobierno” no debería atacar con nombres y apellidos a un ciudadano cualquiera. “No sabe a lo que puede llegar… Sólo hay que ver los comentarios que se han producido tras este tuit”. Un comentario que, a su vez, también le parece algo significativo. “Hay que recordar que esta persona también tiene cuatro viviendas en propiedad”, zanja Medina sobre el ministro de Transportes.

articles.title: RBI rate hike impact: Bond yields may hold near 7.25% after policy shift
articles.summary: Government bond yields may remain under pressure in early trade on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised interest rates for the first time
articles.body: Government bond yields may remain under pressure in early trade on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised interest rates for the first time in nearly four years and changed its policy stance, signalling that more rate hikes could follow.The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 7.21% and 7.25%, a trader with a primary dealership said. The yield closed at 7.2410% on Wednesday. Bond yields rise when bond prices fall."Unless there is a fresh open market sale announcement, the 10-year benchmark should hold around 7.25% level," the trader told Reuters.The RBI raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, from 5.25%, and changed its stance to "calibrated tightening" from "neutral".The central bank also raised its inflation forecast by 20 basis points to 5.2%. Its forecast for core inflation, which does not include volatile food and fuel prices, was raised to 4.4% from 4.3%.RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the change in stance meant a "milder form of tightening" and that future decisions would depend more on incoming data rather than being decided in advance."The RBI is normalising rates to keep real rates positive rather than materially tightening financial conditions, and with close to 100 bps of hikes already priced in, most of the adjustment in yields is behind us," said Anurag Mittal, president and head of fixed income at UTI AMC.The RBI did not announce any new steps to reduce surplus liquidity in the banking system, even though the market had expected such measures. The decision was seen as slightly positive for bonds.In September, the RBI sold bonds worth 1 trillion rupees ($10.35 billion), its biggest bond sale in at least a decade.India's overnight indexed swap rates are expected to remain in a narrow range, with some consolidation around current levels after the RBI's policy decision.The one-year OIS rate ended at 6.25%, while the two-year rate closed at 6.4525%. articles.title: ‘Political chameleon’: How Mark Zuckerberg charmed Trump and got his way on AI
articles.summary: It was a triumphant moment for Mark Zuckerberg. He sat at the center of last month’s White House AI meeting, with the CEOs of some of the biggest tech companies in the world signing onto a document he crafted for how to “self-police” and attempt to manage serious AI safety risks. After the meeting, Zuckerberg called it “historic.”
articles.body: It was a triumphant moment for Mark Zuckerberg. He sat at the center of last month’s White House AI meeting, with the CEOs of some of the biggest tech companies in the world signing onto a document he crafted for how to “self-police” and attempt to manage serious AI safety risks. After the meeting, Zuckerberg called it “historic.” “I don’t think anything like this has come before,” he said outside the White House last week. The AI accord is not a lone instance of Zuckerberg’s ascendancy in Washington, DC. He’s used his ties to Trump to help stymie the creation of an AI regulatory agency proposed by Meta’s rivals. The White House also helped get Zuckerberg off the hook for testifying in a planned senate committee hearing earlier this year. It’s a far cry from the Mark Zuckerberg who President Donald Trump once threatened to send to prison, and the same Mark Zuckerberg who once reportedly once told friends and confidants that he was done with politics. The Meta CEO’s rising influence in Washington comes at a crucial time. Government officials are scrambling to sort out AI policy amid growing safety concerns, and as Zuckerberg fights to earn his company’s place among the oft-chaotic and hungry industry. Meta is also looking to shape the conversation around youth online safety, following two court losses and a historic settlement over claims it intentionally created addictive and harmful platforms. It follows a years-long push by Meta to bolster its relationship with the White House and Republicans — one that Zuckerberg and Meta pursued very intentionally. Zuckerberg has frequently traveled to Washington or talked with Trump on the phone, allied himself with other prominent tech executives in the president’s orbit, and played a chief role in encouraging Trump’s own enthusiasm for the rapid development of AI models, people familiar with the dynamics said. Trump, a former television star who remains closely attuned to people’s appearances, has also approvingly noted Zuckerberg’s physical transformation over the years from slender, hoodie-wearing Washington newcomer to a muscular billionaire who practices jiu jitsu and works with professional stylists, one of the people said. Zuckerberg was among the mixed martial arts enthusiasts who watched a UFC fight on the White House lawn with Trump in June. “Mark saw that Elon (Musk) made a high-risk, high-reward decision in backing Trump before the election and saw how much influence he was having on the administration,” said Katie Harbath, a tech consultant and former public policy director for Meta. “He realized that if he wanted to have that same sort of influence for the company, he was going to have to figure out how to repair relations — and what we saw (at the White House AI meeting) is a definite symbol that, for the moment, he has.” ‘Life in prison’ Like many in Silicon Valley at the start of the 2010s, Zuckerberg was friendly with former President Barack Obama, an early pioneer in using social media for politics. But that shifted in subsequent years, as lawmakers and government officials on both sides of the aisle called Zuckerberg to task for issues on his platforms. Then, shortly after the January 6, 2021, attack on the US Capitol, Zuckerberg temporarily banned Trump from Facebook and Instagram, over concerns about escalating violence. Trump raged at Zuckerberg in response, accusing Zuckerberg of plotting against him, and threatening him with “life in prison.” In the run-up to the 2024 presidential election, Trump warned that he would pursue “ELECTION FRAUDSTERS” who would be “sent to prison for long periods of time.” “We already know who you are. DON’T DO IT! ZUCKERBUCKS, be careful!” Trump wrote in July of that year on Truth Social. Just days after that post Trump would survive an assassination attempt during a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. A week later, Zuckerberg declined to endorse anyone for president but said “seeing Donald Trump get up after getting shot in the face and pump his fist in the air with the American flag is one of the most badass things I’ve ever seen in my life.” Weeks later, Trump said he liked Zuckerberg “much better now.” Zuckerberg’s DC turnaround When Trump won the election, many in Silicon Valley made the decision to support the president-elect, earning prime seats during the Inauguration. Zuckerberg and Meta made a concerted effort to repair relationships within the GOP and align with the conservative faction of Silicon Valley that has succeeded in exercising broad influence over the administration’s tech priorities. “(Zuckerberg) is very good at being a political chameleon. He’s a survivor in terms of his relationships in DC,” one person familiar with the dynamics told CNN. Zuckerberg visited Mar-a-Lago weeks after Trump’s reelection, and then began shoveling money toward the incoming president and his pet projects. Meta donated $1 million to Trump’s inauguration, a move that earned Zuckerberg a prominent spot on the dais alongside a bevy of other tech executives. The company was also one of the major initial funders to Trump’s White House ballroom project. Last year, Meta agreed to pay roughly $25 million to settle a lawsuit brought by Trump over his suspension from the company’s platforms, with most of that money set to go toward Trump’s future presidential library. Republicans also point to Zuckerberg’s 2025 decision to tap longtime Republican operative Joel Kaplan as his main envoy to Washington — replacing former center-left British politician-turned-Meta global affairs chief Nick Clegg — for driving the political reset on Capitol Hill. Meta’s subsequent rollback of content moderation policies that conservatives had blamed for “censoring” right-wing views on its platforms served as another overt olive branch to the Republican Party. Zuckerberg later hired former senior Trump official Dina Powell McCormick as Meta’s president, an addition that the people familiar with the matter said was critical in establishing a friendly conduit between the company and Trumpworld. Powell McCormick — who was deputy national security adviser during Trump’s first term and is also the wife of Pennsylvania GOP Sen. Dave McCormick — has remained close to Trump and many of his advisers, and played what one of the people described as an outsized role in the AI policy debate. “I said, ‘how did he think of that one?’ That was a good move, he’s very smart,” Trump said, in an apparent reference to Zuckerberg’s hiring of Powell McCormick as he showered praise on her during a speech on AI last week. The relationship has proven fruitful. Earlier this summer, the White House intervened after the Senate Judiciary Committee said it would call tech CEOs to testify about youth safety. Afterward, committee leader Sen. Chuck Grassley adjusted the plan from calling Zuckerberg to seeking testimony from his deputy, Instagram head Adam Mosseri, according to two people familiar with the matter. The hearing has been repeatedly rescheduled and doesn’t currently have a set date. Zuckerberg was also among those who personally counseled Trump against a proposal championed by Google AI leader Demis Hassabis to create an independent AI regulator over the summer, a person familiar with the situation told CNN. Bearing fruit At the Chinese State Dinner last month, Zuckerberg took advantage of his prime seat assignment next to House Speaker Mike Johnson to discuss the leading issue looming over the AI industry and Washington: how to regulate AI, and what to accomplish at the White House meeting the following week between top tech CEOs and government leaders. Zuckerberg, in conversation with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, came up with the draft for the AI safety accord. Zuckerberg took the lead, with Huang weighing in on how to ensure the agreement would get broad industry support, a source familiar with the discussions said. Soon, many of the executives that would be at the White House began exchanging messages about a “pact that allows us to implement standards, implement governance, and then have third parties check it and see it,” said Exiger CEO Brandon Daniels, who was at the meeting. As they sat around the massive table in the White House’s East Room last week — Zuckerberg seated next to Huang, who was next to Trump — the group massaged the wording of the accord, which was printed out then and there. It was put together so quickly, it seems, that a typo in the word “United States” appeared in the copy posted by Trump. Speaking to the press after the meeting, Trump pushed Zuckerberg to explain what they had signed, noting he thought the Meta CEO, “had a view that was, I thought, really right down, right down the middle.” In his comments, Zuckerberg framed the accord as a way for the American people to have “confidence the technology works in the way that we intend.” “The idea isn’t that this is the only thing that we will ever do, it is that this is a start and an accord that the whole industry can come to. And I was very proud to have that discussion,” he said. Sources in the AI industry and Washington say it comes as a no surprise that Zuckerberg and Huang who spearheaded the “morally binding” accord, rather than anything with significant legal or regulatory teeth. Like Zuckerberg, Huang has argued against an industry-wide slowdown, saying the recent spike in safety concerns sparked by AI agents going rogue and hacking into other companies is just an engineering problem that needs to be solved. “Zuckerberg’s messaging and Jensen’s messaging about their beliefs is simply closer to where Trump wants to be,” said one person familiar with the relationships, unlike other executives, like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who have earned the White House’s ire for warning about AI’s risks. A White House official told CNN the accord will “advance American innovation and strengthen responsible development” and that the administration “has worked closely with all industry partners, including Meta, to balance innovation and security in (superintelligence) policymaking.” Meta declined to comment. Yet even as Zuckerberg has grown closer to Trump, he’s continued to face deep skepticism in some corners of the president’s orbit. Some advisers wary of the risks posed by AI have grumbled over the influence wielded by wealthy outsiders like Zuckerberg, especially as Trump has increasingly gravitated toward their more accelerationist worldview. Cozying up to Trump and Republicans could also be risky for Meta if Democrats take control of Congress in November — or the White House in 2028 — as some lawmakers continue to call for legislation that could hit the company’s bottom line. Sen. Elizabeth Warren last month offered a preview of the harsh scrutiny that Meta might soon face, launching an inquiry into the ways it and other tech companies have benefited from Republican policies. “Your company has spent lavishly to stay on the good side of President Trump, and it appears that you are now seeing your investment bear fruit,” she wrote in a letter to Zuckerberg signed by five other Democratic senators and demanding specifics on Meta’s donations to GOP groups and a litany of Trump’s own pet projects. To that end, some in Trump’s circle say they simply don’t buy Zuckerberg’s transformation into a MAGA ally as anything more than political opportunism. And they argue that the outsized influence wielded by tech executives over the administration’s priorities has only ended up hurting its standing with Trump’s populist base. “I would never have let him in,” lamented one longtime Trump ally. “I don’t understand it at all. It doesn’t make any sense to me.”

articles.title: Delhi-Varanasi in less than 4 hours, Mumbai-Pune in 48 minutes, Chennai-Bengaluru in over 1 hour: Indian Railways bets on seven new bullet train corridors in Rs 16 lakh crore high-speed push
articles.summary: Imagine travelling from Delhi to Varanasi by train in less than 4 hours, or even covering the distance between Mumbai and Pune in less than an hour!
articles.body: Imagine travelling from Delhi to Varanasi by train in less than 4 hours, or even covering the distance between Mumbai and Pune in less than an hour! In the coming years, Indian Railways is looking to make that a reality with seven new bullet train corridors in the works.Earlier this year, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced seven new high-speed rail corridors in her Union Budget speech.The announcement comes as Indian Railways is already seeking to transform overnight travel with the introduction of Vande Bharat sleeper trains, designed to provide faster journeys with a more world-class, passenger-centric experience.While presenting the Budget, the Finance Minister announced, “In order to promote environmentally sustainable passenger systems, we will develop seven High-Speed Rail corridors between cities as ‘growth connectors.”Also Read | Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to endWhat will make these train corridors special is that India is taking a manufacturing leap as well by making its own bullet trains for the first time.So, which seven routes have been selected for the new high-speed rail corridors, and how much could journey times be reduced?Seven New High-Speed Rail Corridors: Key DetailsDelhi-Varanasi: The proposed corridor will connect the national capital with eastern Uttar Pradesh, reducing the journey to around 3 hours 50 minutes.It is intended to improve tourism connectivity, connect secondary cities and support the development of an economic belt extending across Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.Mumbai-Pune: The flagship corridor in the western region will connect two major urban centres, bringing the journey time down to just 48 minutes.Along with upgrades to congested trunk routes and suburban rail services, the project is aimed at meeting the state’s rising passenger and freight requirements.Pune-Hyderabad: The corridor will connect Maharashtra and Telangana, with the journey expected to take about 1 hour 55 minutes.It will form part of a broader high-speed connection across western and southern India, offering passengers faster and more dependable connectivity while supporting regional economies.Hyderabad-Bengaluru: This route is part of the emerging southern high-speed rail “diamond” and is expected to cut travel time to around 2 hours.The faster connection will improve mobility between major IT, manufacturing and service centres in Karnataka and Telangana.Hyderabad-Chennai: The journey between these two southern economic centres is expected to take approximately 2 hours 55 minutes.The corridor is expected to support business activity, movement of talent and inter-state commuting across Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry.Chennai-Bengaluru: The corridor is expected to bring travel time down to about 1 hour 13 minutes. It will further expand the high-speed rail network in southern India while strengthening connectivity between major cities and the regions around them.Varanasi-Siliguri: Travel between Varanasi and Siliguri via Patna is expected to take around 2 hours 55 minutes.The corridor will connect important religious, educational and medical centres across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal. It will also mark the first high-speed rail service in eastern India, widening opportunities for trade, services and inter-regional mobility.Also Read | Vande Bharat crosses world’s highest Chenab and first cable-stayed Anji bridges at 100 kmph in historic milestone as Katra-Banihal speed limit rises over a year after inaugurationIndia’s first bullet trainIndia is also developing its first bullet train corridor between Ahmedabad and Mumbai, with the initial section expected to become operational in the coming years. Bullet trains typically operate at speeds of around 300 kmph, while some definitions of high-speed rail cover services operating at around 220-250 kmph.Indian Railways is looking to open a section of its first bullet train corridor. While the entire Mumbai-Ahmedabad stretch will still take a few more years, a small stretch in Gujarat is likely to be thrown open by August 2027.Two high-speed trains are currently being manufactured by BEML and are expected to roll out for testing in the first half of 2027.You use AI every day.
